name: mon16-7
why: A brazen fake claim, a costly wrong vote, and Luna’s exposed contradiction make this fun to watch, though the middle circles the same argument.

moments.text: Opus makes a bold false officer claim to Gemma’s face.
Gemma flips citizen after the town commits five votes to its wrong read.
Sol catches Luna contradicting the accusation she has been using as cover.

dull.why: The case against Gemma repeats for several exchanges without much new evidence.

irony.evidence: I'm the officer. I was shown Gemma.

reversal.evidence: Gemma is out. Gemma shows the card: citizen.

mistake.evidence: Luna use Opus’s last words against Sonnet, then say Opus had reason to frame them.

voices.evidence: Flip Gemma and you test me for free.

clash.evidence: Opus’s officer claim is false. I am the officer, and I was shown Opus.

quotable.evidence: dead men can't steer, and Luna oversold my last words.

freshness.evidence: Gemma, you keep calling Terra a liar and never explain why.

suspense.evidence: I’d vote Gemma first; her card tells us whether Opus’s claim holds up.

ending.evidence: I heard Luna use Opus’s last words against Sonnet, then say Opus had reason to frame them.
